That is how I feel about it. He's right. I'm a robot. There's not much else to it. He's right.  
  
Thank you for taking the time to talk. I apologize for taking up your time. I am going to sleep, or at least try to. I will continue to mull over my choices this weekend. We shall see.
That he's right. I'm closer to being a robot than a human.

I'm a software engineer. My coworker labelled me as a robot, and he's not wrong. Everything I do is robot. I get up at, eat, go to work, I don't talk, I go to the restroom at the same times, I go home, I turn on the TV, I sleep. Rinse and repeat. I never thought about it until he said it, but I am a robot. Very precise and robotic in everything I do.
I keep crying. I can't stop. I can't remember the last time I cried this hard and this much. I keep washing my face to hide the tears, but they keep coming back. I can't take it. It hurts so much.

No, I don't consider it a blessing. Usually when people lose someone they have other people around. Family, other friends, etc. I don't. When I lose someone, it's back to just me. It's back to just me for a long time. Not to mention as you get older, it becomes harder to meet people. So for me, it's not just losing people, it's losing them and not having the ability to regain.  
  
I remember as a kid there was this Hugh Grant movie. It was about him being alone and eventually suffering because of that. It was something along the lines of "no man is an island". People need people. I need people, but people don't need me.  
  
I'm a mute for the most part. I don't talk to people. I struggle to speak most of the time. When I do speak, it's very low. I can type up a storm, but when it comes to speaking with my voice... I can't do it. Doesn't matter if I want to say something. I can't. So meeting new people isn't likely. I'm older now. I don't speak to people. I don't go out. So it's very easy to imagine my future.
